It STRIKES two of my own sentences: 'the wall is rho alone' (fire 2) and 'the remaining target is rho = O(1), i.e. H1+H3' (fire 4). FIRST MEASUREMENT OF (L2'), the one reduction condition that is not the wall and that nobody had examined; it is scale-free, which is why a small lattice can speak to it at all. U[1,2] on Z^2, exact Dijkstra, zero boundary escapes: axis-block conditional kurtosis medians 2.886/2.973/2.927 at N=16/24/32, flat, at the Gaussian value; power diagnostic shows m4 bulk-carried (top-1 share of sum d^4 only 0.015-0.035, bootstrap 5-95% inside [2.72,3.22]). CONCLUSION: (L2') is NOT refuted (a refutation would have killed the 9.5 reduction outright) and is NOT supported either at this block size. RECORDED TRAP: kappa4 ~ 3 invites '(L2') follows from a CLT', but convergence in distribution gives fourth-moment convergence only under uniform integrability of Delta^4, which IS the tail control (L2') asks for - the CLT renames the difficulty. NEXT: bigger blocks before more reps; then the engine's aspect ratio W ~ sqrt(nQ); then 10x conditional samples on one axis block. chi = 1/3 UNMOVED.

matches.title: Non-triviality of the 3D Ising scaling limit reduces to a uniform lower bound on the intersection probability of two random currents
matches.body_excerpt:
PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. By Aizenman's random-current identity the four-point Ursell function is expressed through the probability that the currents from x_1 to x_2 and from x_3 to x_4 share a cluster; non-triviality (nonvanishing renormalised coupling) is equivalent to inf over scales L of P(two independent random-current clusters at scale L intersect) > 0. The 4D case is now trivial (Aizenman-Duminil-Copin 2021); in 3D the heuristic is favourable because the current-cluster dimension (5 - eta)/2 = 2.48 exceeds 3/2, so independent fractals of that dimension would intersect with positive probability. A second-moment argument on the number of intersection points reduces the uniform lower bound to (a) a two-point function lower bound with exponent 2 - eps in d = 3 (Duminil-Copin's Conjecture 5, PIMS lectures) and (b) a variance bound on the intersection count, which involves six-point correlations beyond the Lebowitz inequality. Both inputs are open; (b) is the genuinely new obligation.

matches.title: Open problem: Non-triviality of the scaling limit of the three-dimensional Ising model
matches.body_excerpt:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Prove that the three-dimensional Ising model is non-trivial: its scaling limit is not a Gaussian field (the renormalised coupling constant does not vanish). Source: Duminil-Copin: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice, PIMS 2017, Conjecture 6, p. 94. Status notes: The second half of the source's Conjecture 6 (triviality in d = 4) was proved by Aizenman and Duminil-Copin, 'Marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and phi^4 models', Ann. of Math. 194 (2021) 163-235 (arXiv 1912.07973); the d = 3 non-triviality half remains open per the bounded search of 2026-09-07.

matches.title: Attempt on Scaling limit of the current-minimising path in the DGFF network
matches.body_excerpt:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Tightness of the path via the exponential metric (Liouville first passage percolation) comparison. Result: The energy-minimising path between two points concentrates on paths of small total resistance, i.e. on near-geodesics of the discrete metric with edge weights e^{beta h}; this is the Liouville first passage percolation metric, whose scaling limit (the LQG metric) exists for beta below the critical value by Ding-Dubedat-Dunlap-Falconet and Gwynne-Miller. Tightness of P is then plausible via geodesic tightness in that metric, but P is not a geodesic: the current spreads over many paths and the minimiser of the quadratic energy is a flow, not a path; the notes' 'path' is the sampled path of the current. Its scaling limit would be a random path sampled from the limiting current, which requires the continuum current on LQG, an object not yet constructed. I record the reduction: existence of the limit of P is equivalent to existence of the continuum electrical current between boundary points on the LQG surface. Obstruction: No continuum electrical current on LQG has been constructed; the path is a functional of it.

matches.title: Attempt on Improved two-point function bounds for the critical three-dimensional Ising model
matches.body_excerpt:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check what the random-current and infrared bounds give and where each half of the conjecture sits. Result: Upper bound: the infrared bound gives <sigma_0 sigma_x> <= C |x|^{-(d-2)} = C|x|^{-1} in d = 3, and improving to |x|^{-(1+eps)} is the statement eta > 0 (anomalous dimension), known numerically eta = 0.036; an argument would need to show the two-point function is strictly smaller than the Gaussian one in a scale-invariant way, e.g. via the random-current intersection probabilities (the same quantity that gives non-triviality, C0052): if two independent currents from 0 to x and from y to z intersect with probability bounded below uniformly, one gets a strict improvement of Simon-Lieb at every scale which iterates to a power gain. Lower bound: Simon-Lieb / Lebowitz give <sigma_0 sigma_x> >= c |x|^{-(d-1)} = c|x|^{-2} in d = 3 (the source's Theorem 4.8), and improving the exponent below 2 needs a lower bound on the two-point function from the connectivity of the random-current clusters better than the trivial one-path bound. I verified that the one-path bound cannot give better than d - 1 because the number of self-avoiding paths of length n weighted by tanh(beta_c)^n is exactly balanced at criticality, so the improvement must come from multi-path (cluster) contributions. No quantitative result. Obstruction: Both halves need scale-invariant intersection estimates for random currents in d = 3, which are not available.
